slot.brief: Monatomic gas heat added at constant volume; find temperature rise using first law

stem: A rigid vessel contains $4$ mol of an ideal monatomic gas. When $1992$ J of heat is supplied, the temperature of the gas rises by: (Take $R = 8.3$ J mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$.)

verdicts.working: At constant volume, $Q=nC_V\Delta T$, with $C_V=\frac32R$. Thus $\Delta T=1992/[4(\frac32)(8.3)]=40\,\mathrm K$.

working:
$W=0$ at constant volume, so $Q=\Delta U=nC_V\Delta T$. 
$C_V=\dfrac{3}{2}R$ for a monatomic ideal gas.
$\Delta T=\dfrac{1992}{4\times\dfrac{3}{2}\times 8.3}=40$ K.

Independent check: At constant volume, $Q=nC_V\Delta T$, with $C_V=\frac32R$. Thus $\Delta T=1992/[4(\frac32)(8.3)]=40\,\mathrm K$.
solution:
At constant volume, $W=0$, so $Q=nC_V\triangle T$, with $C_V=\frac{3}{2}R$ for a monatomic gas.
$$\triangle T=\frac{1992}{4\times\frac{3}{2}\times 8.3}=40\text{ K}$$
